{{Short description|Type of category in category theory}}
{{refimprove|date=January 2017}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically in the field known as [[category theory]], a [[monoidal category]] where the monoidal ("tensor") product is the [[Product (category theory)|categorical product]] is called a '''cartesian monoidal category'''. Any [[Category (mathematics)|category]] with finite products (a "finite product category") can be thought of as a cartesian monoidal category. In any cartesian monoidal category, the [[Initial and terminal objects|terminal object]] is the monoidal unit. [[Duality (category theory)|Dually]], a monoidal finite coproduct category with the monoidal structure given by the [[coproduct]] and unit the [[Initial and terminal objects|initial object]] is called a '''cocartesian monoidal category''', and any finite coproduct category can be thought of as a cocartesian monoidal category.

Cartesian categories with an internal [[Hom functor]] that is an [[adjoint functor]] to the product are called [[Cartesian closed category|Cartesian closed categories]].<ref>{{nlab|id=cartesian+monoidal+category|title=Cartesian monoidal category}}</ref>

== Properties ==
Cartesian monoidal categories have a number of special and important properties, such as the existence of [[Diagonal morphism|diagonal map]]s Δ<sub>''x''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''x''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''x''&nbsp;⊗&nbsp;''x'' and augmentations ''e''<sub>''x''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''x''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''I'' for any [[Object (category theory)|object]] ''x''. In applications to [[computer science]] we can think of Δ as "duplicating data" and ''e'' as "deleting data". These maps make any object into a [[comonoid]]. In fact, any object in a cartesian monoidal category becomes a comonoid in a unique way.

== Examples ==
Cartesian monoidal categories: 
*'''Set''', the [[category of sets]] with the [[Singleton (mathematics)|singleton set]] serving as the unit.
*'''Cat''', the [[Category of small categories|bicategory of small categories]] with the [[product category]], where the category with one object and only its identity map is the unit. 
Cocartesian monoidal categories: 
*'''Vect''', the [[Category_of_modules#Category_of_vector_spaces|category of vector spaces]] over a given [[field (mathematics)|field]], can be made cocartesian monoidal with the monoidal product given by the [[direct sum of vector spaces]] and the [[Examples of vector spaces#Trivial or zero vector space|trivial vector space]] as unit. 
*'''Ab''', the [[category of abelian groups]], with the [[direct sum of abelian groups]] as monoidal product and the [[trivial group]] as unit. 
* More generally, the category ''R''-'''Mod''' of (left) [[module (mathematics)|module]]s over a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' ([[Commutative ring|commutative]] or not) becomes a cocartesian monoidal category with the [[direct sum of modules]] as tensor product and the [[Zero object (algebra)|trivial module]] as unit.

In each of these categories of modules equipped with a cocartesian monoidal structure, finite products and coproducts coincide (in the sense that the product and coproduct of finitely many objects are isomorphic). Or more formally, if ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''X''<sub>1</sub> ∐ ... ∐ ''X''<sub>''n''</sub> →&nbsp;''X''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;×&nbsp;...&nbsp;×&nbsp;''X''<sub>''n''</sub> is the "canonical" map from the ''n''-ary coproduct of objects ''X''<sub>''j''</sub> to their product, for a [[natural number]] ''n'', in the event that the map ''f'' is an [[isomorphism]], we say that a [[biproduct]] for the objects ''X''<sub>''j''</sub> is an object <math>X = \bigoplus_{j \in {1,\ldots,n}} X_j</math> isomorphic to <math>\coprod_{j\in {1,\ldots,n}}X_j</math> and <math>\prod_{j\in {1,\ldots,n}}X_j</math> together with maps ''i''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''X''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;→&nbsp;''X'' and ''p''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;→ &nbsp;''X''<sub>''j''</sub> such that the pair (''X'',&nbsp;{''i''<sub>''j''</sub>}) is a coproduct diagram for the objects ''X''<sub>''j''</sub> and the pair (''X'',&nbsp;{''p''<sub>''j''</sub>}) is a product diagram for the objects ''X''<sub>''j''</sub> , and where ''p''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;∘&nbsp;''i''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;id<sub>''X''<sub>''j''</sub></sub>. If, in addition, the category in question has a [[zero object]], so that for any objects ''A'' and ''B'' there is a unique map 0<sub>''A'',''B''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''A''&nbsp;→&nbsp;0&nbsp;→&nbsp;''B'', it often follows that  ''p''<sub>''k''</sub>&nbsp;∘&nbsp;''i''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;:&nbsp;''&delta;''<sub>''ij''</sub>, the [[Kronecker delta]], where we interpret 0 and 1 as the 0 maps and identity maps of the objects ''X''<sub>''j''</sub> and ''X''<sub>''k''</sub>, respectively. See [[pre-additive category]] for more.
